entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found within roughly the last 30 days (since mid-September 2026):

---

- **GRPM Anishinaabek exhibit reopened Oct 12, 2026:** 
The Grand Rapids Public Museum reopened its Indigenous history exhibit, now retitled "Anishinaabek: The Original People of This Place," on Monday, October 12, 2026.
 
The reimagined exhibit features new holographic visuals, hands-on experiences, and an immersive interior design.
 
The exhibit also includes three new murals created by West Michigan Indigenous artists.
 (Wood TV8, Oct 12, 2026)

- **GRPM Grand Opening PowWow held Oct 10, 2026:** 
A Grand Opening PowWow was held October 10, 2026 to celebrate the redesigned exhibit, which is centered on the theme "We Are Still Here" and includes natural elements and connections to the Grand River.
 (grpm.org, Oct 2026)

- **Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids publicly back GRB federal recognition, Sep 16, 2026:** 
On September 16, 2026, the Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids issued a statement supporting efforts to reaffirm federal recognition of the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians.
 This adds a new institutional voice to the ongoing recognition campaign. (Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids, Sep 16, 2026)

- **New archaeology book covers Grand River-area Anishinaabe history, published Jan 13, 2026:** 
*The Historical Archaeology of Michigan*, by Dean L. Anderson, Michael S. Nassaney, and Krysta Ryzewski, was published January 13, 2026 by the University Press of Florida; it brings together archaeological research across the state's last 400 years, including findings associated with Anishinaabe peoples.
 
The book highlights Anishinaabe peoples, settler colonialism, immigrants, agriculture, industry, and urbanization.
 (University Press of Florida / Michigan State Historic Preservation Office, 2026)

- **GRPM Community Archives and Research Center (CARC) funding gap, ongoing:** 
The museum is seeking community support to fully fund the CARC renovation after the Federal Administration rescinded a 2024 National Endowment for the Humanities award, with the project targeted for completion in late 2026.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business, 2026)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since mid-September 2026), filtered to exclude anything well established before August 1, 2026:

---

- **Coldbrook/River North RFQ issued, Oct. 7, 2026:** 
The city of Grand Rapids issued a Request for Qualifications to find a development partner for 6.4 acres in the River North neighborhood, covering three adjacent parcels at 1120, 1165, and 1101 Monroe Ave. NW, where the city anticipates "mixed-use, mixed-income development."
 
The city envisions a mixed-use development that could rise five to seven stories.
 
Submissions are due Nov. 16; the city expects to select a development partner in December or January.
 (WOOD-TV, Crain's Grand Rapids Business, Grand Rapids Magazine)

- **State TBP cap doubled, new guidelines approved, Sept. 23, 2026:** 
The Michigan Strategic Fund board approved new guidelines for the Transformational Brownfield Plan program after lawmakers authorized a major expansion; Public Act 36 of 2026, which Gov. Gretchen Whitmer signed into law over the summer, raised the post-construction tax capture cap to $3.2 billion.
 
This essentially doubled the size of the program.
 Grand Rapids riverfront projects, including Fulton and Market, stand to benefit directly. (WOOD-TV, WLNS)

- **West Michigan waterfront developers preparing TBP applications, July 2026:** 
Major waterfront developments in Grand Rapids, Muskegon, and Holland are preparing applications for the expanded Transformational Brownfield Program.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business, July 14, 2026)

- **East Riverfront Park groundbreaking, Aug. 21, 2026:** 
State, city, and community leaders broke ground on the East Riverfront project, a $19 million investment to turn an old industrial site into an accessible green space, located just west of the Acrisure Amphitheater and representing the first major public greenspace investment along the Grand River's southside in generations.
 
Phase 1 includes 4.5 acres of new greenspace, a half-mile non-motorized trail, water access for recreational use, and an access point to the Acrisure Amphitheater; funding sources include ARPA (via Michigan DNR grant to Downtown Grand Rapids Inc.) and the Grand Rapids Downtown Development Authority.
 (City of Grand Rapids)

- **Grand River Restoration Lower Reach construction underway, June 2026:** 
In June 2026, the Grand River Restoration Lower Reach broke ground, extending from Fulton Street to Bridge Street in the heart of downtown; key elements include removal of four low-head dams to eliminate dangerous hydraulics and improve public safety.
 This is post-August 1 confirmation that active construction is ongoing. (Experience GR)

- **GSA auctioned former Navy/Marine Corps Reserve riverfront property, May 20, 2026:** 
The GSA announced the auction of the former Navy and Marine Corps Reserve Center in Grand Rapids, saying the sale will save taxpayers nearly $350

entries.body:

Here are the findings, filtered to only genuinely new or changed information from approximately the last 30 days (mid-September to mid-October 2026). Note that the MDHHS Eat Safe Fish Guide update (June 2026) and the EGLE/whitewater rapids permit story (Dec 2024, with federal funding finalized March 2026) predate the August 1, 2026 River Brain baseline and are excluded. One item, the September 10 DNR regulation update, falls just outside the 30-day window but is the most recent regulatory change found and is flagged accordingly.

---

- 
**DNR trout, salmon, and sturgeon regulation update, Sept. 10, 2026:** The Michigan NRC approved updated inland trout, salmon, and lake sturgeon regulations now in effect, including clarified possession limits, identification of current fish communities, and alignment of select rules with Wisconsin to ease enforcement for anglers on shared boundary waters.
 (Michigan DNR Newsroom)

- 
**Grand River Muskellunge size limit confirmed in force:** Under Fisheries Order FO-206.26, the minimum size limit for Muskellunge on the Grand River downstream from the Sixth Street Dam (both Kent and Ottawa counties, including Lake Macatawa) remains 46 inches.
 This order took effect April 1, 2026, and no further amendment has been found. (Michigan DNR / NRC)

- 
**No flood watches or river advisories at Grand Rapids gauge, as of Sept. 17, 2026:** NOAA's gauge at Grand Rapids (GDRM4) reported no active watches, warnings, or advisories.
 (NOAA Water Prediction)

- 
**Low river stage at Grand Rapids gauge, Oct. 12, 2026:** The USGS gauge at Grand Rapids recorded a streamflow of approximately 2,240 ft³/s and a river stage of 2.19 ft as of today.
 (RiverApp / USGS)

- No new EGLE permit actions, MDHHS Eat Safe Fish advisories specific to the Grand River through Grand Rapids, or public health contact advisories for the Grand River in Kent County were found within the last 30 days. The most recent public health advisory found was a sewage-discharge "no body contact" notice for the Grand River in Ottawa County (M-45 Bridge to 68th Ave.), issued Feb. 19, 2026, which predates the baseline. (WWMT / Ottawa County Public Health)

entries.title: Events and community
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found since the August 1, 2026 base date:

---

- 
**Lower Reach restoration, active boulder placement, Oct. 7, 2026:** Construction Equipment Guide (CEG) reported Oct. 7 that Taplin Group is actively placing more than 125 scattered habitat boulders in the river using a Komatsu excavator and NPK grapple; the Lower Reach plan removes four low-head dams and replaces them with two channel-wide grade-control structures, with construction expected to conclude fall 2027.
 (Construction Equipment Guide)

- 
**One-month construction check-in, early Aug. 2026:** WZZM13 published a "one month in" update noting the Grand River Restoration is "the most-watched construction project in Grand Rapids," with active work continuing near Ah-Nab-Awen Park.
 (WZZM13)

- 
**Mayors' Grand River Cleanup, Sept. 19, 2026:** WMEAC held the annual kickoff at Sixth Street Bridge Park on Sept. 19; last year's event removed over 11,500 pounds of garbage, with this year's volunteers working multiple watershed sites.
 (Fox17)

- 
**2026 Mayors' Cleanup totals posted (WMEAC site, updated ~Sept. 2026):** WMEAC's page now shows 11,600 lbs of trash removed "this year," with 500-plus volunteers, 6 cities, 35 sites, and 12-plus miles of river cleaned at the Sept. 19 kickoff at Sixth Street Park.
 (WMEAC)

- 
**Grand River Network project page updated, ~Oct. 1, 2026:** The Grand River Network's projects page (updated approx. 11 days ago) now lists the Thornapple River Pedestrian Bridge and Grand Rapids Public Museum as "recently completed," and shows the Cannonsburg Trail, Pettis Ave. Trail North, and Northland Tunnel all "under construction" with fall 2026 completion goals.
 (Grand River Network)

- 
**Acrisure Amphitheater noise ruling, Sept. 5, 2026:** A judge issued a ruling on the Acrisure Amphitheater concert noise dispute; MLive published a transcript of the judge's explanation on Sept. 5, 2026, following complaints raised at a city meeting in June 2026.
 (MLive)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days (since ~September 12, 2026), plus a few items from the past 60–90 days that post-date the August 1 baseline:

---

- **Snuffbox mussel, DNR stocking, Sept. 25, 2026:** 
About 7,500 captive-reared snuffbox mussels were released into three waters in southeastern Michigan, announced by the Michigan DNR in late September 2026; 1,000 of them carry passive integrated transponder (PIT) tags to enable RFID-based follow-up surveys.
 
Approximately 2,800 mussels went to the Clinton River, over 4,100 to the Huron River, and 500 to Cass Lake.
 Note: these are not Grand River sites, but the stocking program directly parallels ongoing Grand River snuffbox recovery work.

- **Lake sturgeon, genetics breakthrough, Sept. 28–30, 2026:** 
LSSU researchers refined a genetic testing method that makes sex determination in sturgeon more reliable, a useful tool for fisheries research, conservation, and aquaculture; findings were published Sept. 3 in BioTechniques.
 
The breakthrough could aid conservation and fisheries management by reducing handling time and allowing researchers to analyze archived samples.


- **Salmon and steelhead runs, Grand River, as of Oct. 12, 2026:** 
The Grand River (Kent and Ottawa Counties) is currently at peak run status, high confidence, for Kings, Coho, and Steelhead, at 60°F water temperature and 2,040 cfs flow, with peak expected to end approximately Oct. 12.


- **Invasive carp barrier, Sept. 29–30, 2026:** 
Great Lakes lawmakers argue that recent construction pauses are especially concerning after hundreds of juvenile silver carp were found just 80 miles from Lake Michigan, warning that an invasion could damage native fisheries, ecosystems, and billions of dollars in fishing and boating-related economic activity.
 
In July, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers paused work for the second time on the $1.15 billion Brandon Road Interbasin Project that aims to block invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes.
 
While that most recent stop-work order was lifted this month, legislators wrote that the delays are increasing the already hefty price tag of the project.


- **Sea lamprey barrier, Upper Reach EIS, Grand River, ongoing:** 
The 6th Street Dam will not be removed until a new lamprey barrier is constructed, a project still being studied by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; the GLFC aquatic connectivity coordinator stated a project design is not expected to be selected until approximately 2028.
 
More than $20 million in federal funding has already been secured for the future barrier project.


- **Invasive species, Grand River corridor, April–May 2026 (new since baseline):** 
Lesser celandine (*Ficaria verna*) is already widely established along the Grand River corridor and is actively spreading in Lower Michigan and southeastern Wisconsin.

entries.title: Construction progress
entries.body:
Now let me search for anything specifically from the last 30 days (mid-September to mid-October 2026) to isolate truly new information.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found from roughly the last 30 days (mid-September to October 12, 2026). Most major milestones (contract award, groundbreaking, Ah-Nab-Awen closure, July 1 in-water start, EIS scoping) were already established before the August 1, 2026 base date or shortly after. The following bullets reflect only information that is new or more specific than what would have been known as of August 1, 2026:

---

- 
**Lower Reach in-water construction confirmed actively underway as of late September 2026:** A September 30, 2026 report confirmed crews began work July 1, installed a large coffer dam to isolate roughly half the river flow, and removed the first low-head dam; Executive Director Matt Chapman expected two of four dams to be removed by end of summer. (CitizenPortal.ai / Talking Michigan Transportation podcast, Sep 30, 2026)


- 
**First dam nearly half removed, original limestone rapids evidence uncovered:** About one month into physical work, crews had removed nearly half of the first low-head dam and during excavation uncovered limestone bedrock with flow patterns they believe are evidence of the original historic rapids. (Fox17, ~July 31, 2026)


- 
**Active boulder placement documented October 7, 2026:** Construction Equipment Guide (Midwest Edition, Oct 7, 2026) documented Taplin Group actively placing boulders using a Komatsu excavator with NPK grapple; the Lower Reach design calls for more than 125 scattered habitat boulders, with a sandbag cofferdam managing river flow during work. (Construction Equipment Guide, Oct 7, 2026)


- 
**Upper Reach sea lamprey barrier EIS timeline refined:** Great Lakes Fishery Commission aquatic connectivity coordinator Lisa Walter stated the agency is "probably looking at 2028" until a project design is selected for the new barrier; more than $20 million in federal funding has already been secured for the future barrier project. (Spartan Newsroom / Bridge Michigan, Jul 31, 2026)


- 
**Upper Reach EIS public comment period closed; draft EIS target set for July 2027:** The Great Lakes Fishery Commission and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers officially resumed the EIS process in spring 2026; a public scoping meeting was held April 22 and the 30-day comment period closed May 22, 2026; a draft EIS is now anticipated in July 2027. (Grand Rapids WhiteWater, site updated ~June 2026)


- 
**Lower Reach completion target confirmed as end of 2027:** The City of Grand Rapids officially stated construction of the Lower Reach will be completed by end of 2027, pending weather and river conditions. (WWMT, Jul 1, 2026)

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Now let me do a targeted follow-up search for the most recent news from the last 30 days specifically on the DNR September regulation changes and the Grand River restoration groundbreaking.
Here are the findings, filtered to information that is genuinely new or changed since the August 1, 2026 base research date:

---

- **Michigan DNR Fisheries Order 254 update, September 10, 2026 (Michigan DNR):** 
Fisheries Order 254, governing inland lake trout and salmon regulations, was updated by the NRC to clarify possession limits and better reflect current fish communities in affected waters.
 
Some waters had their previous trout fishing regulations removed as no longer appropriate, shifting management focus to warmwater species better suited to current conditions.
 No changes specific to the Grand River were cited in this order.

- **DNR inland trout, salmon, and sturgeon regulation package effective, September 10, 2026 (Michigan DNR):** 
A broader package of regulation changes for inland trout, salmon, and lake sturgeon took effect following NRC action, including clarifying possession limits and aligning certain fishing rules with Wisconsin to simplify enforcement for anglers on shared boundary waters.


- **Grand River Lower Reach construction underway as of July 1, 2026 (WWMT, Spartan Newsroom):** 
Dam removal work began July 1, 2026,
 following the June 1 groundbreaking. 
An unresolved element flagged as of late July 2026 is the Sixth Street Dam, which serves as a barrier preventing invasive sea lamprey from moving upstream,
 with no final decision yet on its future.

- **Sea lamprey barrier question still open, July 31, 2026 (Spartan Newsroom / Capital News Service):** 
As of July 31, 2026, city leaders had launched the rapids restoration but the question of how to keep invasive sea lamprey out while restoring natural flow remained unresolved.
 
Details and timelines for the Upper Reach, from Ann Street to Bridge Street, including possible Sixth Street Dam removal and a new sea lamprey barrier, are still to come.


- **No new MDHHS Eat Safe Fish advisories specific to the Grand River found post-August 1, 2026.** The 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guides were released June 8, 2026, predating the base research cutoff. No subsequent advisory updates or changes for Grand River waterbodies were found in the last 30 days.

- **No new EGLE permits or public health advisories for the Grand River in Grand Rapids were found in the last 30 days.** The most recent EGLE permit action (December 2024) and federal USDA funding authorization (March 2026) both predate the base research cutoff.

entries.title: Events and community
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently confirmed items for the River Brain, focused on activity from roughly the last 30 days (since Aug 1, 2026 base date). Most substantive river developments found date from earlier in 2026 and are not included as new. One cleanup result and one festival result post-date the base:

---

- 
WMEAC's 2026 Mayors' Grand River Cleanup kicked off Sept. 19 at Sixth Street Park, with 500+ volunteers, 6 participating cities, and 7,200+ lbs of trash removed across 35 sites and 12+ miles of river (WMEAC).


- 
DGRI's fifth annual Return to the River festival was held Aug. 22 and 23 in the River North neighborhood, with a space-themed "cosmic adventure" concept reflected in art installations, riverwalk activities, and live music (Downtown Grand Rapids Inc.).


- 
The Grand River Restoration Lower Reach groundbreaking occurred in June 2026, covering the Fulton Street to Bridge Street corridor; key elements include removal of four low-head dams to eliminate dangerous hydraulics (Experience Grand Rapids).


- 
On the Upper Reach, a formal NRCS funding agreement was signed in May 2026, the Great Lakes Fishery Commission and Army Corps officially resumed the EIS process in spring 2026, and a draft EIS is now anticipated in July 2027 (Grand Rapids Whitewater).


- 
The Grand River Network reported a $125M Greenway construction push this season, projected to deliver 255 acres of public riverfront space, with the South Rogue River Trail and Grand Rapids Public Museum riverfront among active projects (Grand River Network, April 1, 2026).


- 
The Bayou Segment of the Idema Explorers Trail in Robinson Township (Ottawa County) has been completed, described as a major milestone in the West Michigan trail network and finalizing the Grand Crossings Loop (Grand River Greenway, 2026).

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days, filtered to what is relevant to the Grand River system:

---

- **Snuffbox mussel stocking (Oct. 7, 2026):** 
Michigan DNR, working with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and U.S. Geological Survey, stocked 7,500 snuffbox mussels at multiple sites on the Huron River (Livingston County), the Clinton River, and Cass Lake (Oakland County).
 
Of those, 1,000 received PIT tags, 1,000 received physical shell tags with unique identifiers, and the remainder received color markings, allowing researchers to track survival, reproduction, movement, and impacts from invasive zebra and quagga mussels.
 (Outdoor News / WHMI, Oct. 7, 2026)

- **Lake sturgeon genetics breakthrough (Sep. 30, 2026):** 
Michigan researchers refined genetic testing that can more reliably determine the sex of lake sturgeon, particularly in young fish and outside the spawning season, which could reduce handling time and allow analysis of archived samples for conservation and fisheries management.
 (Great Lakes Commission / MLive, Sep. 30, 2026)

- **Grand River salmon run at peak (Oct. 7, 2026):** 
The Grand River (Kent and Ottawa Counties) is currently at peak run status with high confidence, carrying kings, coho, and steelhead at a water temperature of 65°F and a flow of 2,690 cfs (low and steady); peak typically ends around Oct. 12.
 (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub, Oct. 7, 2026)

- **Steelhead mass-marking program shift (Sep. 22, 2026):** 
The USFWS Great Lakes Mass Marking Program shifted its emphasis from steelhead to coho salmon in 2025; yearling steelhead stocked in 2025 were mass-marked with an adipose fin clip and coded wire tag, but the 2026 stocking cohort was not subject to mass marking.
 
Around 90% of steelhead caught in Prairie Creek and the upper Grand have been wild fish in recent years.
 (Michigan Sea Grant / Great Lakes Angler Diary, Sep. 22, 2026)

- **Invasive silver carp juvenile spawning event near Lake Michigan; Brandon Road barrier halted (Aug. 17, 2026):** 
Sampling crews removed hundreds of small silver carp, 4 to 6 inches long, from the Marseilles Pool just 80 miles from Lake Michigan, with the presence of juveniles indicating a spawning event occurred possibly even further upriver.
 
In late July, the Army Corps of Engineers issued a stop work order on construction of the Brandon Road Interbasin Project, noting the project was under administrative review.
 
No reason has been given for the stoppage, despite repeated information requests from the bipartisan Congressional Great Lakes Task Force, state agencies, and various Great Lakes organizations.
 (WTTW / Alliance for the Great Lakes, Aug. 17–26, 2026)

entries.title: Construction progress
entries.body:
Now let me search for the most recent news (last 30 days, roughly September 7 to October 7, 2026) to find anything genuinely new:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found from roughly the last 30 days (September 7 to October 7, 2026):

---

- **Lower Reach dam removal and boulder placement actively underway as of late September 2026:** 
After nearly 20 years of planning, crews began in-water work this summer; Executive Director Matt Chapman confirmed crews started July 1, installed a large cofferdam to isolate roughly half the river flow, and removed the first low-head dam, with two of four dams expected out by end of summer.
 
Chapman noted that "for the first time in over 100 years, you can actually hear rapids roaring in downtown Grand Rapids again."
 (Sept. 30, 2026, Citizen Portal / Talking Michigan Transportation podcast)

- **Nearly half of Dam 1 removed by late July; original limestone rapids bedrock uncovered:** 
Nearly a month into physical work, nearly half of one dam had been removed and boulders were already being placed in designed spots; during excavation, crews uncovered a chunk of limestone believed to be remnant of the original historic rapids.
 
Crews also noted the dry summer kept water levels low and helped accelerate the work schedule.
 (approx. Aug. 1, 2026, Fox17)

- **Construction Equipment Guide feature confirms boulder placement ongoing, fall 2027 target holds:** 
The October 7, 2026 Midwest Edition of Construction Equipment Guide shows a Komatsu excavator with an NPK grapple placing boulders in the Grand River; construction is expected to span two seasons and conclude in fall 2027, depending on water levels and weather.
 (Oct. 7, 2026, Construction Equipment Guide)

- **Upper Reach EIS timeline: design selection now estimated at 2028:** 
The Sixth Street Dam will not be removed until a new barrier is constructed; Lisa Walter, aquatic connectivity coordinator for the Great Lakes Fishery Commission, stated the Army Corps EIS process means "we're looking at probably 2028 until we have a project design selected."
 
More than $20 million in federal funding has already been secured for the future barrier project.

- **Ah-Nab-Awen Park closure ongoing through project end:**
